ISCR ~500 W/kg array-level and >100 kW compute per launched tonne is a single-source design target: one unrefereed preprint (arXiv 2604.07760) plus one startup patent bet; no hardware, no replication

High-voltage arrays are established heritage, regime-bounded: ISS 160 V chosen for cable mass; direct-drive SEP runs 300-400 V because 400 kW at 100-160 V means up to 4,000 A distribution; LEO plasma arcing fences the regime out of constellation altitudes
Starlink standardization lesson confirmed independently: silicon beats GaAs at Starlink-class production economics; cell choice is second-order behind panel standardization and production cadence

The qualification moat is priced: $4.5M S-111A+S-112A campaign (STRATFI), ~$800/h beam time with ~33% of facility requests unsatisfied, GSFC-STD-1000H mandate, incumbents sell qualification as the product; the fast-campaign counter-position is unclaimed

evidence.paraphrase: ISCR concept: solar cells, vapor-chamber radiator, and compute on common support; ~500 W/kg at array level; >100 kW compute per launched tonne; 16 MW / 150 t / 20 m x 2,200 m grid of 16,000 panels in one Starship; >30% energy/token gain at 35 C vs 105 C junction; unrefereed preprint
Sophia Space patent bet on radiator-area orbital data centers; article notes the ISCR preprint is not peer reviewed
ISS 160 V primary power chosen explicitly to reduce cable mass
High-power SEP direct-drive at 300-400 V; at 400 kW a 100-160 V bus must distribute up to 4,000 A
High-voltage solar array arc testing for direct-drive Hall thruster (D2HET) operation
Degradation of high-voltage solar arrays due to arcing in the LEO plasma environment
EDDA H2020 direct-drive spacecraft power hardware test results
Silicon's mass and cost advantage at Starlink-class production outweighs GaAs efficiency for 30 kW-1 MW space datacenter payloads
GaAs prohibitively expensive at Starlink production volume; standardization and cadence dominate cell choice
RHA beam time ~$800/h; most cost in test-bench development; ~33% of facility requests unsatisfied
GSFC-STD-1000H mandates AIAA S-111A / S-112A qualification by rule
Rocket Lab sells cells 'fully qualified to AIAA-S111-2014' — qualification as the product feature

operations.reason: R6 (system architecture as research) decomposes into four sub-directions with distinct evidence classes: ISCR integration is a single unrefereed preprint plus one startup patent bet (design target, not demonstrated); high-voltage arrays are established heritage bounded out of LEO by plasma arcing; Starlink panel standardization is confirmed directionally by two independent analyses (cell choice second-order to cadence); qualification economics are priced — $4.5M S-111A+S-112A campaign, $800/h beam, 33% unsatisfied demand, standards mandate, incumbents sell qualification as the product — and the fast-campaign counter-position is unclaimed. Cheapest high-information artifact: benchtop cell-on-vapor-chamber panel through thermal-vacuum.

operations.method: 4-track in-session web sweep (delegation workers remain network-denied and repo-read-only, so sweeps run in-session with WebSearch/FetchURL). Tracks: (1) ISCR integrated solar-compute-radiator claims and commercial parallels, (2) high-voltage array heritage and the LEO plasma constraint, (3) Starlink-class panel standardization economics, (4) qualification campaign cost structure and mandates.
operations.result: 1 problem, 12 sources, 4 claims, 20 relations, 1 assessment (established-with-gap); problem mapped to chokepoint-germanium. Perimeter: ISCR is preprint-only (no referee, no hardware); SemiAnalysis and Ex Terra are analyst pieces, not primary disclosures — no published Starlink BOM teardown; STRATFI $4.5M anchor carried from R2 event ev-000000000007, not re-admitted; SCTC papers are conference proceedings.
